Automation.Api.UnsafeWebhooksWarning: Starting the API will enable webhooks that call external services:
Autosave.FailureDueToFullDisk: Autosave failed due to insufficient disk space
Bot.BeaversPerished: Don’t even get me started on the beavers.They had it all. Fresh air, clean water.Now they’re just a faint memory.
Breeding.NutrientBringing: Nutrients are brought by haulers, the unemployed, and workers after work.
BuilderPriorityTool.Description: Use this tool to set priority for construction, demolition and gathering goods from Rubbles.
BuilderPriorityTool.Tip: Click an item to set its priority or hold the button to select a bigger area.
Building.AdvancedBreedingPod.Description: Utilizes an advanced breeding process to produce adult beavers, eager to get to work.
Building.AdvancedBreedingPod.FlavorDescr: The idea came up when a kit fell into a cauldron full of extract and had a giant growth spurt after drinking it all.
Building.Agora.Description: A large gathering place where beavers can discuss timber-related topics.
Building.Agora.FlavorDescription: When the green beacons are lit, it's a sign for Folktails to gather.
Building.AncientAquiferDrill.FlavorDescr: Humans' last ditch attempt to recover what was lost.
Building.AquaticFarmhouse.Description: Employs specialized farmers to plant and harvest <YellowHighlight>Aquatic</YellowHighlight> crops.
Building.AquaticFarmhouse.FlavorDescript: "There was once a rumour we eat fish. Disgusting!" —Ma' Ngonel
Building.Aquifer.FlavorDescription: It's not difficult to find when it's so loud.
Building.AquiferDrill.FlavorDescription: Unlike beavers, it's built to let water flow.
Building.BadtideDrain.Description: Spews out badwater during a Badtide.
Building.BadtideDrain.FlavorDescription: "Is that what hoomans used pipes for? Bleh." —Pina.
Building.BadwaterDischarge.Description: Seals a Badwater Source. Can be opened or closed. When open, badwater flows even during droughts.
Building.BadwaterDischarge.FlavorDescrip: Only real civil engineers are allowed nearby.
Building.BadwaterDome.Description: Seals a Badwater Source. Can be opened or closed at will.
Building.BadwaterPump.Description: A reinforced pump capable of pumping out badwater. Low badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Building.BadwaterPump.FlavorDescription: "I wish the extra protective measures included nose plugs." —Suli
Building.BadwaterRig.Description: Seals a Badwater Source. Employs workers who extract badwater directly from the source.
Building.BadwaterRig.FlavorDescription: Those working on top of a boiling badwater source feel constant pressure.
Building.BadwaterSeep.Description: A source of badwater with limited pressure.
Building.BadwaterSource.FlavorDescriptio: "Why do we have to clean up the hoomans' mess? Oh, right, they're all dead." —Pina
Building.Bakery.Description: Bakes bread and pastries from different flours.
Building.Bakery.FlavorDescription: "Nothing like a hot bun with a little sawdust sprinkled on top." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.Barrack.FlavorDescription: "Two Folktails walk into a barrack." —Iron Teeth joke
Building.BeaverBust.Description: A bust of an important looking beaver.
Building.BeaverBust.FlavorDescription: Mischievous kits like to add various details to the Ol' Kazko's face.
Building.BeaverStatue.Description.Folkta: A statue of a well-fed beaver.
Building.BeaverStatue.Description.IronTe: A statue of a hard-working beaver.
Making you proud in the good years and hungry in the bad.
The original design with a sickle was deemed too Folktails-like.
Building.Beehive.Description: Boosts the growth of nearby crops.
Building.Beehive.FlavorDescription: "You get used to the buzzing eventually."  —Ma' Ngonel
Building.Bell.Description: It rings at the beginning and the end of a workday.
Building.Bell.FlavorDescription: "It's the morning ringing you should be looking forward to." —Ol' Kazko
Building.Bench.FlavorDescription: Every now and then, some vandal will eat on the public property.
Building.Blockage.Description: A natural barrier blocking water. Can be demolished.
Building.Blockage.FlavorDescription: It's a wonder that nature creates something on par with beaver engineering.
Building.BotAssembler.Description: Assembles autonomous bots to perform everyday tasks.
Building.BotAssembler.FlavorDescription: It all started with a simple "what if I didn't have to work today". —Pina
Building.BotPartFactory.FlavorDescriptio: "Done! Wait, what is this screw doing here?" —Pina
Building.Brazier.Description: A blazing fire safely contained in a decorative enclosure.
Building.BrazierOfBonding.FlavorDescript: "If not for us, then for the future generations." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.BreedingPod.Description: The Iron Teeth's preferred, and only, way to reproduce.
Building.BreedingPod.FlavorDescription: "Kits are our future. We need twelve more by next month." —Ol' Kazko
Building.BuildersHut.FlavorDescription: Beaverome wasn't built in a day. Legend says it was six hours.
Building.BulletinPole.Description: A decorative pole for public messages.
Building.BulletinPole.FlavorDescription: Have you been injured at work? You may be eligible for compensation! Contact Suli.
Building.Campfire.Description: A place for beavers to relax and socialize in the evening.
Building.Campfire.FlavorDescription: Sometimes, fire and wood are a good match.
Building.Carousel.Description: A wooden merry-go-round for beavers of all ages.
Building.Carousel.FlavorDescription: "Where do you think you're going, kit? These branches won't peel themselves." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.Centrifuge.Description: Heavy duty machinery transforming the dangerous badwater into usable extract.
Building.Centrifuge.FlavorDescription: The idea came up after a Folktails carousel ran too fast.
Building.ChargingStation.Description: A place where bots come to recharge.
Building.ChargingStation.FlavorDescripti: Do not use with non-Ironbot devices.
Building.Chronometer.Description: Sends a signal based on the time of day.
Building.CoffeeBrewery.FlavorDescription: Were it not for consumption limits, the Iron Teeth would not sleep at all.
Building.CompactWaterWheel.Description: A compact generator transforming flow of water into power.
Building.CompactWaterWheel.FlavorDescrip: Yes, you can reinvent the water wheel.
Building.ContaminationBarrier.Descriptio: Stops soil contamination from spreading beneath it.
Building.ContaminationBarrier.FlavorDesc: "Build a barrier a day, keep badtides away!" —motivational poster
Building.ContaminationSensor.Description: Measures water contamination below its arm.
Building.ContemplationSpot.Description: A small spot where beavers can contemplate nature.
Building.ContemplationSpot.FlavorDescrip: Beavers spend some quiet time here, pondering the whims of mother nature.
Building.ControlTower.Description: A tall structure that sends out a signal to nearby bots to boost their performance.
Building.ControlTower.FlavorDescription: A bot must obey orders given it by beaver beings except where beavers are no more.
Building.Dam.Description: Blocks water but allows some to pass through a spillway at the top.
Building.Dam.FlavorDescription: As everyone knows, a civilization's fundaments are built underwater.
Building.DanceHall.Description: An open hall where beavers can let their tails loose.
Building.DanceHall.FlavorDescription: "Come on, don't just stand there like some Iron Teeth bore." —Suli
Building.DecontaminationPod.Description: A bath for beavers to recover from badwater exposure.
Building.DecontaminationPod.FlavorDescri: "No Suli, you can't drink the extract. You fell into the cauldron when you was a kit!" —Ma 'Ngonel
Building.DecorativeClock.Description: A decorative timepiece large enough to be read by grandfathers.
Building.DecorativeClock.FlavorDescripti: It's difficult to imagine that in the olden times, beavers used clepsydras.
Building.DeepBadwaterPump.FlavorDescript: The extended pipe helps with both height differences and the smell.
Building.DeepWaterPump.Description: Pumps and filters water for beavers to drink. Badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Building.DeepWaterPump.FlavorDescription: "The water comes from the land down under, where cattails grow and beaver's a plumber." —Iron Teeth work song
Building.DepthSensor.Description: Measures water depth below its arm.
Building.Detailer.Folktails.FlavorDescri: Make your tail tell a tale.
Building.Detailer.IronTeeth.FlavorDescri: Come on, it doesn't hurt to get one. —Suli
Building.DirtExcavator.Description: A heavy duty mining rig for collecting dirt. It will continue to produce dirt even after reaching the bedrock.
Building.Discharge.FlavorDescription: Give me enough buckets and I shall move the lake. —Ol' Kazko
Building.DistrictCenter.Description: Establishes a district with its own population, goods and an isolated path network. Employs builders.
Building.DistrictCrossing.Description: Balances goods between the two connected districts. Each side has workers who distribute goods between the District Crossing and the rest of the district.
Building.DistrictCrossing.FlavorDescript: Why did a beaver cross a district?
Building.DoubleDynamite.FlavorDescriptio: When extreme measures weren't extreme enough.
Building.DoubleFloodgate.FlavorDescripti: How do you improve upon perfection? You make it taller.
Building.DoubleLodge.Description: A bigger lodge that fits more beavers.
Building.DoublePlatform.FlavorDescriptio: Double the height, same trademark sturdiness.
Building.DoubleShower.FlavorDescription: "I liked my yesterday's shower buddy better." —Pina
Building.Dynamite.Description: Destroys the terrain underneath it and triggers adjacent dynamites.
Building.Dynamite.FlavorDescription: Some extreme measures were needed to adapt to the post-apocalyptic world.
Building.EarthRecultivator.Folktails.Des: Distributes tree seeds across the Earth. When launched, makes the beavers in the area extra happy.
Building.EarthRepopulator.IronTeeth.Desc: Launches pioneers to distant lands. When launched, makes the beavers in the area extra happy.
Building.EarthRepopulator.IronTeeth.Flav: After some now-classified tests with a catapult, this design was adopted instead.
Building.EfficientFarmhouse.Description: Employs farmers to plant and harvest crops. The expanded Folktails design fits more farmers.
Building.EfficientFarmhouse.FlavorDescri: The efficiency depends on the "no eating at work" policy.
Building.EfficientMine.Description: Employs miners who extract scrap metal from Underground Ruins. Innovative design maximizes mining speed.
Building.EfficientMine.FlavorDescription: The Iron Teeth gained the upper paw by being the first to survey underground.
Building.ExercisePlaza.Description: An area designated for structured group routines to build core strength and flexibility.
Building.ExercisePlaza.FlavorDescription: The Iron Teeth want to be like their creations - always harder, better, faster, stronger.
Building.ExplosivesFactory.FlavorDescrip: As if building the whole settlement out of wood wasn't enough.
Building.FarmerMonument.FlavorDescriptio: Taming the wasteland, feeding the people.
Building.Farmhouse.Description: Employs farmers that plant and harvest crops.
Building.Farmhouse.FlavorDescription: Agriculture is one of the pillars on which today's beaver society stands.
Building.Fermenter.Description: Ferments plants to produce nutritious food.
Building.Fermenter.FlavorDescription: Following a few incidents, the list of products allowed for fermentation is limited.
Building.FillValve.Description: A one-way outlet that regulates the downstream water level.
Building.FireworkLauncher.Heading: Heading: {0}
Building.FlameOfUnity.FlavorDescription: "Nothing unites as efficiently as production quotas." —Ol' Kazko
Building.Floodgate.Description: Blocks water up to an adjustable height.
Building.Floodgate.FlavorDescription: No-one thought you could improve on a dam until Ol' Kazko created The First Floodgate.
Building.FlowSensor.Description: Measures water flow below its arm.
Building.FoodFactory.FlavorDescription: Before this, taking a quick bite at work often resulted in structural damage.
Building.Forester.FlavorDescription: Bold and beautiful, foresters are the core of beaver society.
Building.FountainOfJoy.FlavorDescription: It's not a waste if it makes you happy.
Building.GathererFlag.FlavorDescription: By putting berries in a basket, beavers accidentally came up with a tasty dessert.
Building.GearWorkshop.FlavorDescription: "Wooden gear's solid!" was a catchphrase coined by Ol' Kazko as he pushed for rapid industrialization.
Building.GeothermalEngine.Description: A large turbine that harnesses a Geothermal Field to generate power.
Building.GeothermalEngine.FlavorDescript: It's unmanned mostly because of the smell.
Building.GeothermalField.Description: A source of constant, free power that can be harnessed with the right contraption.
Building.GeothermalField.FlavorDescripti: Is it green energy when it's yellow?
Building.GravityBattery.Description: Stores power surplus and gives it back when its network is underpowered. The higher it is built, the more power it can store.
Building.GravityBattery.FlavorDescriptio: Here's what you can do when you invent your own laws of physics.
Building.GreaseFactory.Description: A factory that produces slippery grease that makes bot machinery run smoother.
Building.GreaseFactory.FlavorDescription: "Well, a bot could be systematic, hydromatic... Why couldn't it be greased?" —Ol' Kazko
Building.Grill.FlavorDescription: "Mash 'em, boil 'em, grill 'em on a non-stick pan!" —"500 Ways to Eat a Potato" by Ma' Ngonel
Building.Gristmill.Description: Grinds roots and seeds into flour.
Building.Gristmill.FlavorDescription: More refined tastes gave rise to more refined foods.
Building.Hammock.FlavorDescription: They used to be tied to trees, until a few too many tree cutting accidents.
Building.HaulingPost.Description: Haulers assist workers within a district in carrying goods, greatly increasing their productivity.
Building.HaulingPost.FlavorDescription: The most muscular of all beavers, you don't want to step on a hauler's tail.
Building.Hedge.FlavorDescription: No hedge maze is a challenge when you can just chew through.
Building.Herbalist.Description: Creates antidote that cures contaminated beavers.
Building.Herbalist.FlavorDescription: The brewing apparatus is used strictly for medical purposes.
Building.HttpAdapter.Description: Turns its input signal into an API endpoint and webhook calls, whatever that means.
Building.HttpLever.Description: An API-controlled lever. Humans left a lot of those lying around.
Building.HydroponicGarden.Description: Cultivates plants not suited to outdoor farming.
Building.HydroponicGarden.FlavorDescript: The idea was born after a discovery of damp hooman ruins covered in rapidly growing fungus.
Building.ImpermeableFloor.Description: A floor panel that stops water from leaking through it.
Building.ImpermeableFloor.FlavorDescript: It all started with one beaver getting fed up with the sound of a leaking roof.
Building.Indicator.Description: An indicator light with alerting capabilities.
Building.Indicator.JournalEntryWhenSwitc: Add journal entry when switched on
Building.IndustrialLumberMill.Descriptio: Makes planks from logs. Its innovative design fits more workers in the same amount of space.
Building.IndustrialLumberMill.FlavorDesc: Two saws are better than one.
Building.Inventor.FlavorDescription: Inspired by the legacy of Ol' Kazko, beaver inventors are always eager to improve their timbertech.
Building.IrrigationBarrier.Description: Stops soil irrigation and contamination from spreading beneath it.
Building.IrrigationBarrier.FlavorDescrip: The Iron Teeth are happy to control every aspect of life in the desert.
Building.LaborerMonument.FlavorDescripti: Even after manual labor gave way to industrialization, Iron Teeth's work ethos hasn't changed.
Building.Lantern.FlavorDescription: Nocturnal by nature, modern beavers do feel a little anxious when it's dark.
Building.LargeIndustrialPile.FlavorDescr: What's better than a pile? A pile of piles.
Building.LargePile.FlavorDescription: Sadly, nobody is keeping a log of how much wood comes in and out.
Building.LargePowerWheel.Description: A beaver-operated source of power, redesigned to employ multiple workers.
Building.LargePowerWheel.FlavorDescripti: The Iron Teeth wanted their own carousel.
Building.LargeRelic.FlavorDescription: "Some hoomans were so big they ate from these." —Suli
Building.LargeRowhouse.FlavorDescription: The Iron Teeth have developed a high building complex.
Building.LargeTank.FlavorDescription: Despite the efforts of kits trying to use it as a swimming pool, this tank was designed for industrial use.
Building.LargeWarehouse.FlavorDescriptio: With so much goods packed inside, there's no room to swing a tail.
Building.LargeWaterPump.Description: Pumps and filters large amounts of water for beavers to drink. Badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Building.LargeWaterPump.FlavorDescriptio: "With the reservoir of water, we can drink every day." —"The Shores of Beaver Bay"
Building.LargeWaterWheel.Description: A bigger, more efficient water wheel. Supported from the side.
Building.LargeWaterWheel.FlavorDescripti: "You're gonna need a bigger wheel." —Ol' Kazko
Building.LargeWindTurbine.Description: Generates more power proportional to wind speed.
Building.Levee.FlavorDescription: Balanced, reinforced, and shaped to perfection by generations of beaver water engineers, this is not "just a block of wood".
Building.Lever.Description: Sends a manually controlled signal. A great first step toward automating a settlement.
Building.Lido.Description: A perfect place to relax by a river.
Building.Lido.FlavorDescription: To celebrate their kits' first swim, beavers throw a pool party.
Building.Lodge.Description: A place to spend the night.
Building.Lodge.FlavorDescription: "In the olden days a lodge was just that, a lodge. And now? I don't know about that." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.LumberMill.FlavorDescription: Encouraged by Ol’ Kazko, mechanized wood processing caused much gnashing of teeth among older beavers.
Building.LumberjackFlag.Description: Employs a lumberjack that cuts trees.
Building.LumberjackFlag.FlavorDescriptio: "They are lumberjacks and that's the way, they sleep all night and they work all day!" —Popular beaver song
Building.MechanicalFluidPump.Description: Pumps water or badwater up on one side and discharges them on the other. More efficient than a regular pump.
Building.MechanicalFluidPump.FlavorDescr: Better running water than running with buckets.
Building.MedicalBed.Description: Injured beavers lie here to rest and heal.
Building.MedicalBed.FlavorDescription: "Tis but a scratch. May I go back to work?" —Pina
Building.MediumRelic.FlavorDescription: "You can sometimes see these fall from the sky." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.MediumTank.FlavorDescription: After The Great Drought, beavers made it a rule to always have a few of these around.
Building.MediumWarehouse.FlavorDescripti: Proper storage of goods is crucial to surviving the hazards of a post-apocalyptic world.
Building.Memory.Description: Changes and holds its state in response to specific input sequences. A cornerstone of advanced automation.
Building.MetalFence.Description: A decorative fence made from metal.
Building.MetalFence.FlavorDescription: Beware the beaver who prefers metal to wood.
Building.MetalPlatform.FlavorDescription: "This table looked smaller in the catalog." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.MetalPlatform3x3.Description: A metal platform supported by a sturdy central column.
Building.MetalPlatform5x5.Description: A large metal platform supported by a sturdy central column.
Building.Metalsmith.Description: Manufactures simple metal parts from scrap metal.
Building.Metalsmith.FlavorDescription: "If you want it to last, make it metal. That's one thing hoomans did well." —Ol' Kazko
Building.Mine.Description: Employs miners who extract scrap metal from Underground Ruins.
Building.Mine.FlavorDescription: No such thing as delving too greedily and too deep.
Building.MiniLodge.Description: A small lodge for a single beaver.
Building.Motivatorium.Description: A mechanical theater that teaches the core Iron Teeth values.
Building.Motivatorium.FlavorDescription: "Day after day, night after night, we struggle. It’s beautiful." —Ol' Kazko
Building.MudBath.Description: A mud bath mechanically infused with bubbles.
Building.MudBath.FlavorDescription: Where are the bubbles coming from?
Building.MudPit.FlavorDescription: This is where kits build their first little dams.
Building.NaturalDam.Description: A natural barrier that blocks water but allows some to pass through a spillway at the top. Can be demolished.
Building.NaturalDam.FlavorDescription: It's hard to believe there were simpler times when mud with branches constituted a dam.
Building.NaturalOverhang.Description: A protruding rock platform that acts as a bridge or a foundation. It is watertight.
Building.NaturalOverhang.FlavorDescripti: "Just make sure there's water below before you jump!" —Suli
Building.Numbercruncher.Description: A complicated machine that solves calculations without beavers operating it.
Building.Numbercruncher.FlavorDescriptio: Far superior to the now retired Digitchewer.
Building.Observatory.Description: By exploring the stars, beavers gain more knowledge about the world they live in.
Building.Observatory.FlavorDescription: The logical next step after stargazing at the campfire.
Building.OilPress.Description: Squeezes oil out of suitable plants.
Building.OilPress.FlavorDescription: Curious kits use it to squash anything from cookies to pine cones.
Building.Overhang.Description: A protruding platform which can act as a bridge or a foundation for other buildings.
Building.Overhang.FlavorDescription: "Oh, looks like we're building a stairway to the clouds. It makes me wonder..." —Pina
Building.PaperMill.FlavorDescription: What originated as a dried snack for scavengers, quickly found multiple other uses.
Building.Path.Description: Buildings must be connected by paths.
Building.Path.FlavorDescription: "Country roads, take me home, to the lodge I belong." —Popular beaver song
Building.PlankFence.Description: A decorative fence made out of planks.
Building.Platform.Description: A raised platform which can act as a bridge or a foundation for other buildings.
Building.Platform.FlavorDescription: Impressive load carrying capacity of beaver platforms makes them masterpieces of engineering.
Building.PoleBanner.FlavorDescription: It was raised up to prevent kits from vandalising the pictures.
Building.PopulationCounter.Description: Monitors various population, housing, and workforce metrics.
Building.PowerWheel.Description: A beaver-operated backup source of power.
Building.PowerWheel.FlavorDescription: Beavers quickly realized they could borrow some techniques from less advanced rodents.
Building.PrintingPress.FlavorDescription: Usually, beavers consume each page right after reading, so good literature is always in demand.
Building.Refinery.Description: Produces various types of fuel for bots.
Building.Relay.Description: Performs simple logical operations on its input signals.
Building.Relic.Description: Ancient technology that can be demolished for a burst of Science.
Building.ReservePile.FlavorDescription: "Old wood is the best. They grew it differently back then." —Ma' Ngonel
Building.ReserveTank.FlavorDescription: "Yes, it was sealed. Yes, it is fine to drink. You first." —Pina
Building.ReserveWarehouse.FlavorDescript: A gift from the generations past.
Building.ResourceCounter.Description: Sends a signal based on the stock level of the specified good.
Building.Roof.FlavorDescription: A fancier roof is often enough to fuel a friendly neighbourhood rivalry.
Building.RooftopTerrace.Description: A raised terrace where beavers can socialize and appreciate the view.
Building.RooftopTerrace.FlavorDescriptio: A great place to talk the night away, and what a view!
Building.Rowhouse.Description: Practical, shared housing with a small footprint.
Building.Ruins.Description: A limited supply of Scrap Metal.
Building.Ruins.FlavorDescription: Scattered throughout the land, decrepit human ruins provided beavers with the unimaginable - a good superior to wood.
Building.Scarecrow.Description: A field decoration once meant to scare birds now brings delight to young and old alike.
Building.ScavengerFlag.Description: Scavengers collect scrap metal from Ruins.
Building.ScavengerFlag.FlavorDescription: Bringing metal to traditionally wooden settlements, scavengers earn respect from some and disdain from others.
Building.ScienceCounter.Description: Sends a signal based on Science Points.
Building.Scratcher.Description: A machine for scratching those hard-to-reach itches.
Building.Scratcher.FlavorDescription: Even when relaxing, the Iron Teeth are itching to get back to work.
Building.Shower.Description: A refreshing blast of river water to wet one's fur.
Building.Shower.FlavorDescription: Makes conquering the wasteland easier to bear.
Building.Shrub.FlavorDescription: To keep things practical, decorations should be both pretty and tasty.
Building.Slope.FlavorDescription: Whoever put it here, beavers are grateful.
Building.Sluice.FlavorDescription: "Suli, did you forget to flush the badwater again?" —Ma' Ngonel
Building.SmallIndustrialPile.FlavorDescr: "So, they slapped a roof on top and called it industrial. Classic." —Pina
Building.SmallPile.FlavorDescription: No self-respecting individual dumps building materials on the ground.
Building.SmallRelic.FlavorDescription: "Suli! Do not point it at the sun!" —Ol' Kazko
Building.SmallTank.FlavorDescription: Learning how to save every drop of water helped beavers adapt to the harsh environment.
Building.SmallWarehouse.FlavorDescriptio: "No dynamite in my pantry, please and thank you." —Ma 'Ngonel
Building.Smelter.Description: Smelts scrap metal into metal blocks.
Building.Smelter.FlavorDescription: The new beaver world is forged in sweat and smell of burnt fur.
Building.SpiralStairs.FlavorDescription: "If you go through too many, your head will keep spinning!" —Suli
Building.Stairs.FlavorDescription: With the invention of stairs, beavers ascended to the next level.
Building.SteamEngine.FlavorDescription: As great as this invention is, it became a splinter in the side of beaver nations other than Iron Teeth.
Building.StreamGauge.Description: An old-fashioned way to measure water depth, flow and contamination.
Building.StreamGauge.FlavorDescription: There is a tide in the affairs of beavers. Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune.
Building.SuspensionBridge.Description: Allows beavers to pass over gaps.
Building.SwimmingPoll.FlavorDescription: "That's a really good time but we should work on your tailstroke!" —Pina
Building.SwimmingPool.Description: Cordoned lanes for providing a submerged full-body workout without interference.
Building.TappersShack.Description: Employs tappers who gather sap and syrup from trees.
Building.TappersShack.FlavorDescription: Kits are taught early that every droplet matters — be it water or resin.
Building.TeethGrindstone.FlavorDescripti: All part of the daily grind.
Building.TerrainBlock.Description: An artificial block of terrain. Construction order follows the arrows on top.
Building.Thorns.Description: An impenetrable obstacle that also blocks irrigation and contamination. It's difficult to demolish and can injure those who attempt it.
Building.Thorns.FlavorDescription: It's no nature's bounty, only its anger.
Building.Timer.Description: Applies time-based processing to its input signal.
Building.Timer.Mode.Accumulator.Descript: On if <YellowHighlight>{0}</YellowHighlight> is on for a total of at least <YellowHighlight>{1}</YellowHighlight>.
Building.Timer.Mode.Oscillator.Descripti: Alternates between on and off while <YellowHighlight>{0}</YellowHighlight> is on.
Building.Timer.Mode.Random.Description: Randomizes state every <YellowHighlight>{1}</YellowHighlight> while <YellowHighlight>{0}</YellowHighlight> is on.
Building.TributeToIngenuity.FlavorDescri: "Of course it has a purpose. It impresses." —Ol' Kazko
Building.TripleDynamite.FlavorDescriptio: When even extremely extreme mesaures weren't extreme enough.
Building.TripleFloodgate.FlavorDescripti: Any taller and water becomes too heavy to hold back.
Building.TripleLodge.FlavorDescription: "Go forth and multiply" is an adage Folktails take seriously.
Building.TriplePlatform.FlavorDescriptio: Gnawing on poles is strictly prohibited!
Building.Tubeway.Description: A fast, if cramped, means of beaver transportation.
Building.Tubeway.FlavorDescription: Two beavers colliding headfirst is cited as a source of some of the wackiest Iron Teeth inventions.
Building.TubewayStation.Description: A Tubeway network entrance and exit.
Building.TubewayStation.FlavorDescriptio: Claustrophobic beavers are advised to choose a path instead.
Building.Tunnel.Description: Tunnels through terrain, replacing it with a Platform. Use the Layer tool to see under terrain or structures.
Building.UndergroundPile.FlavorDescripti: All the storage space is worth the flight of stairs.
Building.UndergroundRuins.Description: Buried ruins full of metal scraps to be mined.
Building.UndergroundRuins.FlavorDescript: Whatever hoomans were doing down there, it sure required lots of metal.
Building.UnstableCore.Description: An old device that will inevitably explode.
Building.Valve.Description: A one-way water outlet with adjustable flow rate.
Building.VerticalPowerShaft.FlavorDescri: Helps when power consumption goes up.
Building.VerticalTubeway.Description: A fast, if cramped, means of beaver transportation. Connects upward.
Building.VerticalTubeway.FlavorDescripti: Go up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, back, ahead. Hm, you're right where you started.
Building.WaterPump.Description: Pumps and filters water for beavers to drink. Badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Building.WaterPump.FlavorDescription: A gulp of fresh water gets you pumped.
Building.WaterSeep.Description: A source of water with limited pressure.
Building.WaterWheel.Description: Produces power, should be placed in flowing water along a river bank.
Building.WeatherStation.Description: Sends a signal based on the weather.
Building.Weathervane.Description: A small vane that indicates wind direction and strength.
Building.Weathervane.FlavorDescription: "If I am right, this thing could fly if fixed to an engine and a pair of wings." —Pina
Building.WindTunnel.Description: A machine capable of lifting beavers off the ground for extreme experiences.
Building.WindTunnel.FlavorDescription: "I believe I can fly. I just need to work out the escape velocity." —Ol' Kazko
Building.WindTurbine.Description: Generates power proportional to wind speed.
Building.WindTurbine.FlavorDescription: "All we are is sawdust in the wind!" —Folktails song
Building.WoodFence.Description: A decorative fence made from wood.
Building.WoodFence.FlavorDescription: It's like a dam but for beavers.
Building.WoodWorkshop.Description: Strengthens planks by infusing them with resin.
Building.WoodWorkshop.FlavorDescription: Why are treated planks so strong? Because resins.
Building.ZiplineBeam.Description: A horizontal beam bearing zipline cables between stations.
Building.ZiplinePylon.Description: A tower bearing zipline cables between stations.
Building.ZiplinePylon.FlavorDescription: It's common courtesy to smack each other's tail when passing another beaver.
Building.ZiplineStation.Description: A quick and thrilling mode of travel.
Building.ZiplineStation.FlavorDescriptio: "To ride, your tail must be this long." —Sign at the entrance

Experimental.WelcomeText: This version of Timberborn gives you access to prototype, unfinished features. As such, it is also much more likely to include serious bugs. You are a brave beaver indeed.Experimental saves are stored separately from the main game. Updates are likely to break saves compatibility.In this Experimental Mode <RedHighlight>many parts of the game are not translated and are shown in English</RedHighlight>, regardless of your language selection. This allows us to add new content and make quick changes without waiting for time-consuming translations.We highly recommend that you join our official Discord server and participate in the discussion about the new content.
Faction.Folktails.Description: Easygoing but hardworking, Folktails are expert farmers. They respect nature and it rewards them with plentiful bounties.Their motto: Comfort, food, and sturdy wood.
Faction.Folktails.GameOver.Flavor: When you fail to use nature's gifts, it takes them back.
Faction.Folktails.GameOver.Message: Your Folktails met the sad fate of their human predecessors. This is the end.
Faction.Folktails.WonderCompletionFlavor: Having collected great wealth and knowledge, your beavers shared fruits of their labour with the suffering planet. There's still much to do, but Earth may flourish once again.
Faction.Folktails.WonderCompletionMessag: Congratulations! You mastered Folktails' nature-oriented ways and used this map's resources to build the faction's wonder.
Faction.IronTeeth.Description: Defectors of the traditional timber ways, they mastered iron and science to build advanced machinery.They achieve progress through ingenuity, efficiency, and disregard for the environment. Their motto: Work hard, work hard.
Faction.IronTeeth.GameOver.Flavor: Sometimes, the tiniest faulty part breaks the entire machine.
Faction.IronTeeth.GameOver.Message: Your Iron Teeth settlement fell without a chance for recovery. This is the end.
Faction.IronTeeth.WonderCompletionFlavor: Your pioneers flew away over the wasteland, leaving the thriving settlement behind them. If Earth is to recover, the new-found beaver prosperity needed to be shared.
Faction.IronTeeth.WonderCompletionMessag: Well done! Your technological prowess allowed you to utilize the industrious strengths of the Iron Teeth to conquer this map and build the faction's wonder.

MapMetadata.Beaverome.Description: To build the legendary metropolis, the beavers' ancestors drained seven mighty craters. Even with today's timbertech, that's no small feat.
MapMetadata.Beaverome.Name: Beaverome
MapMetadata.Canyon.Description: In the desert, beavers seek valleys where rivers still flow. Easily dammed, this canyon will become a safe haven for all.
MapMetadata.Canyon.Name: Canyon
MapMetadata.Cliffside.Description: The remains of ancient hooman architecture stand scattered across this secluded valley. The beavers aspire to leave a similar mark on the world.
MapMetadata.Cliffside.Name: Cliffside
MapMetadata.Craters.Description: Nobody knows how the craters came to be. Preliminary excavations suggest hoomans' violent involvement.
MapMetadata.Craters.Name: Craters
MapMetadata.Diorama.Description: Before they're allowed to oversee large colonies, aspiring builders are tasked with running small-scale projects like this one.
MapMetadata.Diorama.Name: Diorama
MapMetadata.HelixMountain.Description: Even though they find the riverbed shape impractical, the beavers acknowledge hoomanity's limited water engineering skills.
MapMetadata.HelixMountain.Name: Helix Mountain
MapMetadata.Hollows.Description: These bountiful hollows are a prime area for prospective settlers. The carved out landscape hides many opportunities - the eldest beavers even whisper of buried treasures.
MapMetadata.Hollows.Name: Hollows
MapMetadata.Lakes.Description: These days, areas rich in lakes and rivers are scarce. What little remains shows that there is still hope for Earth.
MapMetadata.Lakes.Name: Lakes
MapMetadata.Meander.Description: Beaver engineers are keen to exploit the natural curvature of the river banks. Planning out the best usage of limited space is the tricky part.
MapMetadata.Meander.Name: Meander
MapMetadata.MountainRange.Description: In the desperate search for fresh water, beavers are ready to climb even the highest mountains.
MapMetadata.MountainRange.Name: Mountain Range
MapMetadata.NotUpdatedDescription: <RedHighlight>This map is not compatible with the experimental branch yet!</RedHighlight>
MapMetadata.Oasis.Description: A lone green refuge in the wasteland surrounded by aquifers that can be accessed by clever beaver engineering.
MapMetadata.Oasis.Name: Oasis
MapMetadata.Plains.Description: With expansive areas as flat as a beaver's tail, this region makes for a safe testing ground for novice engineers.
MapMetadata.Plains.Name: Plains
MapMetadata.Pressure.Description: Creative plumbing is the first skill a wasteland beaver has to learn.
MapMetadata.Pressure.Name: Pressure
MapMetadata.Spillage.Description: This slope is full of small, irrigated enclaves. However, dangers abound in the region - should you not be careful, those areas will become anything but hospitable.
MapMetadata.Spillage.Name: Spillage
MapMetadata.Terraces.Description: Many societies choose to settle on elevated areas, utilizing the beavers' newfound knack for vertical building.
MapMetadata.Terraces.Name: Terraces
MapMetadata.ThousandIslands.Description: Even for natural born swimmers, turning an archipelago into a thriving industrial colony is no easy task.
MapMetadata.ThousandIslands.Name: Thousand Islands
MapMetadata.Waterfalls.Description: It's an old parenting trick to tell kits that a waterfall is just a big floodgate. Here, they will spend weeks looking for a shutoff lever.
MapMetadata.Waterfalls.Name: Waterfalls

NaturalResource.Birch.FlavorDescription: "Remember, kits, do not peel too much bark off! It harms the tree!" —Ma' Ngonel
NaturalResource.Blueberry.FlavorDescript: "You'll come asking for more of these when the drought hits." —Ma' Ngonel
NaturalResource.Canola.FlavorDescription: The best excuse to grow flowers in an Iron Teeth settlement.
NaturalResource.Carrot.FlavorDescription: Raw carrots help beavers balance their diet without giving up on the joy of crunching.
NaturalResource.Cassava.FlavorDescriptio: Poisonous when raw, cassava prompted the Iron Teeth to experiment with fermentation.
NaturalResource.Cattail.FlavorDescriptio: "I know all about tails but what is a cat?" —Pina
NaturalResource.ChestnutTree.FlavorDescr: "May you step on a chestnut!" —Beavers' harshest insult
NaturalResource.Coffee.FlavorDescription: Ancient beavers chewed the beans for an energy boost, the Iron Teeth brewed up a better idea.
NaturalResource.Corn.FlavorDescription: "Nothing good comes from kits playing in the corn." —Ma' Ngonel
NaturalResource.Dandelion.FlavorDescript: In beaver fairy tales, dandelions are known for their melodic voices.
NaturalResource.Kohlrabi.FlavorDescripti: Tastes like paper, crunches like driftwood.
NaturalResource.Mangrove.FlavorDescripti: The seeds were brought by travelers from faraway lands where rivers never dry out.
NaturalResource.Maple.FlavorDescription: Tapped maple produces syrup but high quality timber is an even sweeter reward.
NaturalResource.Oak.FlavorDescription: The best beaver constructions are all oak and iron bound.
NaturalResource.Pine.FlavorDescription: "Oh, mighty forest, how I pine for thee!" —Unknown beaver poet
NaturalResource.Potato.FlavorDescription: "There's more than one way to cook a potato." —Beaver proverb
NaturalResource.Soybean.FlavorDescriptio: Hard and water-resistant, its seeds are perfect toys for kits.
NaturalResource.Spadderdock.FlavorDescri: The nature sends its message through the leaves' shape.
NaturalResource.Sunflower.FlavorDescript: Beavers grow these to show they’re not afraid of the burning sun.
NaturalResource.Wheat.FlavorDescription: "You'll forget the sun in the cloudless sky as we walk in fields of gold." —Beaver ballad

NewGameConfigurationPanel.NormalModeDesc: You want a challenge.Your settlement starts with moderate resources.Droughts and badtides are milder at the beginning but intensify over time.

Tutorial.Badtides.Description: Your settlement has weathered its first badtide.                               Like droughts, badtides are part of the seasonal cycle.                                Future badtides won't be as forgiving, so stay sharp.
Tutorial.Basics.ManagePause: The game can be paused at any moment, helping you assess the situation and plan things out.
Tutorial.Basics.ManageSpeed: You can also increase game speed to reduce downtime while your beavers are working or sleeping.
Tutorial.Basics.MoveCamera: First, let's have a look around the area.
Tutorial.Basics.ZoomCamera: If you want to check on your beavers up close, or get a wider view of the settlement, you can!
Tutorial.Dams.BuildDam: Storing water in tanks keeps your beavers hydrated, but long-term survival depends on taming the flow of water.                        Build a line of Dams across the nearest river, from bank to bank, and observe what happens.
Tutorial.DisablePrompt: Are you sure you want to disable the tutorial?You can re-enable it later in settings.
Tutorial.Droughts.Description: Congratulations! Your settlement has survived its first drought.                               Droughts are part of the seasonal cycle. They will return and become longer over time.If you haven't already, start preparing for the next one by building a dam.
Tutorial.Forestry.Forester: Beavers need a stable source of Logs. Duh.                            Using Science Points produced by your Inventor, unlock the Forester. Then build it in an area where you want to plant trees.
Tutorial.Forestry.MarkBirchesForPlanting: Use the Plant Trees and Bushes tool to plant some Birches. They grow quickly, making them a good choice in a fledgling settlement.                                          Similarly to crops, trees only grow on irrigated, green areas.                                          Remember to mark the planting areas for cutting.
Tutorial.HaulersAndWorkforce.BuildHaulin: As your settlement grows, it processes larger amounts of goods. Transporting them takes a significant part of your workers' day.                                               Haulers help with that. They move the goods around their entire district, following the demand.                                               Let's build a Hauling Post now.
Tutorial.HaulersAndWorkforce.ChangeWorkf: Some workplaces, like Hauling Posts, don't fill all of their worker slots by default. You can change the number of desired workers in a building's panel.                                              Also, you can control how buildings are staffed using workplace priorities. For example, the Hauling Post can usually be set to lower workplace priority.                                              Let's try it now.
Tutorial.HaulersAndWorkforce.PauseHaulin: You can pause buildings and construction sites. This gives you more control over the beavers' actions.                                               For example, paused workplaces are vacated automatically and workers re-assign themselves to other available workplaces.                                               Select the Hauling Post and pause it by clicking the button in its panel.
Tutorial.Housing.Lodges: Two beavers are better than one! Houses improve your beavers' well-being and allow your Folktails population to grow.                                      Beavers automatically assign themselves to available housing slots.
Tutorial.Introduction.Description: Welcome to Timberborn! This tutorial will help you set your paw in the wasteland and survive the first days.                                   You will learn how to use the tools needed to build a thriving beaver community.                                   As you progress through the next steps, the tips will appear here.
Tutorial.LayerTool.ChangeUsingMouse: You can control the visible layer without clicking the buttons with customizable key bindings.                                     Many other actions have key bindings as well. You can find them in tooltips or in the Settings menu.
Tutorial.LayerTool.ChangeUsingUI: As your settlement grows vertically, working beneath buildings and terrain can become difficult.                                  The Layer tool helps with that by hiding everything above the selected layer.                                  Let's change the visible layer by clicking the highlighted buttons.
Tutorial.MoreBeavers.GrowPopulation: Beavers do not reproduce unless there are empty housing slots available. Folktails need two adults and an empty slot for the magic to happen.                                              Tip: Beaver children are called kits.
Tutorial.PowerAndPlanks.LumberMill: It is time to start producing Planks!                                    Build a Lumber Mill directly next to the Water Wheel. You may also build it further away and connect it to the Water Wheel using Power Shafts.                                    Tip: Many buildings, such as Lumber Mills and Lodges, pass power to one another when placed wall to wall. No Power Shafts needed!
Tutorial.PowerAndPlanks.WaterWheel: More advanced buildings require power, and beavers like their power to come from the river.                                    Place a Water Wheel in flowing water along the river bank.
Tutorial.Science.Inventor: Beavers are the engineers of the animal world. It's time to turn their lumberpunk ideas into reality.                           Build an Inventor to produce Science Points.
Tutorial.Science.SciencePoints: For now, let the Inventor work.                                Once you accumulate enough Science Points, we'll spend them to unlock more advanced buildings.
Tutorial.Storage.Pile: Many buildings have some built-in storage but it fills up quickly.                               Build a Large Pile to store more Logs.                               Each storage building holds a single good. You can set the stored good after selecting the building.
Tutorial.Storage.Tanks: All liquids are stored in tanks. This includes the water we've been pumping.
Tutorial.Storage.Warehouses: Finally, let's prepare some storage for Berries. We should also get ready for the upcoming Carrot harvest.                             Food, just like many other boxed goods, is stored in warehouses.
Tutorial.VerticalArchitecture.BuildRooft: In the wasteland, it's important to optimize use of space. Beavers do that by growing their cities vertically.                                                   Some buildings, like Lodges, have flat roofs that can support other structures.                                                   Let's build a Rooftop Terrace now. You may need to use Stairs to connect it to the district.
Tutorial.WaterAndFood.Farmhouse: In the long run, we need something more nutritious. Build a farmhouse to plant and harvest crops.                                 Like flags, a farmhouse has a limited range.                                 Tip: If you are running low on workers, you can pause some buildings. To do so, select a building and click the pause button.
Tutorial.WaterAndFood.Gatherer: In addition to water, beavers need food.                                Gatherers automatically gather Berries within the Gatherer Flag's range. You can see the range when placing the flag.                                Build a Gatherer Flag near some Blueberry Bushes.
Tutorial.WaterAndFood.MarkCarrots: Farmers do not start working until you tell them what and where to plant.                                   Use the Plant Crops tool to designate a Carrot field.                                   Crops need to be planted on irrigated, green land. Otherwise, plants will dry out and eventually die.
Tutorial.WaterAndFood.WaterPump: Beavers need water to survive.                                 Build a Water Pump to ensure continuous access to drinking water. Remember to connect the Pump to the District Center.
Tutorial.Wellbeing.Beaver: You can see the impact your actions have on your beavers.                           Select a beaver by clicking on it. In the panel, you can see its current well-being, attributes, and needs.                           Some needs can reach negative values and incur severe penalties or cause death.
Tutorial.Wellbeing.Campfire: Well-being is a metric that shows how content a beaver is. It affects three attributes: working speed, movement speed, and lifespan.                             One of the main ways of increasing the well-being is through attractions. Attractions are buildings that beavers enter when not at work.
Tutorial.Wellbeing.SelectBeaver: Select a beaver and check its needs
Tutorial.Wellbeing.SetWorkingHours: Remember that beavers need free time to eat, drink, sleep, and enjoy the settlement's attractions.                                    To maximize productivity, you need to balance workers' well-being and their working hours.                                    For now, let's return to the default working hours.
Tutorial.Wellbeing.Shrub: Well-being also increases around decorations. Beavers do not intentionally approach them, so place the decorations close to where your settlers hang out.                          A Shrub is the simplest decoration, and beavers appreciate every bit of greenery.
Tutorial.Wellbeing.WellbeingPanel: For beavers, it's the entire society that counts. You can see your settlement's average well-being in the top left corner of your screen.                                   Click on it to see the fulfillment of all possible needs. There are many ways to make life in the wasteland more bearable.
Tutorial.Wood.ConnectLumberjacks: Every building with an entrance must be connected to a District Center with a Path. When you select a building, you can see its entrance marked by an arrow.                                  Build Paths to connect the Lumberjack Flags to the District Center.
Tutorial.Wood.FinishLumberjacks: The Flags will not be built unless they are in the district's building range.                                 Select the District Center to see its building range. You can extend it by connecting Paths to the District Center's entrance.
Tutorial.Wood.MarkTrees: Lumberjacks only cut trees in areas that you mark for cutting.                         The trees must be within a Lumberjack Flag's range. Select a flag to see its range.                         Use the Mark Tree Cutting Area tool now. Hold the mouse button to select multiple tiles at once.
Tutorial.Wood.PlaceLumberjacks: Every beaver settlement needs Logs, and lots of them. Only lumberjacks cut trees.                                 Build Lumberjack Flags next to nearby trees.
Tutorial.WorkingHours.SetWorkingHours: Adjusting working hours is one way to manage your settlement.                                       Longer workdays mean faster progress, but every evening, beavers need time to relax and sleep. Don't push them too hard for too long.                                       For now, let's increase the working hours just a little.
